lines.text: Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. [level, knowing] Amy gets a dimmer.

lines.text: Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [direct, distracted] Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. [quick, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.text: Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.
lines.script: [goofy, proud] Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? [brisk, pleased] Both. Correct. Go get 'em.

lines.text: Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?
lines.script: [beaming, direct] Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. [puzzled, wary] Also, why are you sticky?

lines.text: Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, bragging] Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. [smug, level] Before lunch.

lines.text: Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.
lines.script: [level, amused] Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. [direct, pleased] I got a truck and two girls. [dry, sincere] Living the song.

lines.text: Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. [proud, level] It was a playoff game. [grim, flat] We lost.

lines.text: Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.
lines.script: [soft, sincere] Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. [proud, amused] And I built that deck.

lines.text: Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.
lines.script: [level, matter-of-fact] Long Island born. Country music raised. [amused, dry] Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.

lines.text: Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.
lines.script: [hyped, bright] Big game tonight. [gleeful, level] If you hear yelling, that's me. [mock-serious, deadpan] If you hear crying, that's also me.

lines.text: Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.
lines.script: [calm, level] Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. [sheepish, rueful] I know. It's on the list.

lines.text: Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.
lines.script: [low, conspiratorial] Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. [tired, flat] That's allowed. [dry, certain] It's in the contract.

lines.text: If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.
lines.script: [warning, deadpan] If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. [flat, grave] Every lunch in there has a name on it. [firm, dry] Read the labels.

lines.text: Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.
lines.script: [exhausted, relieved] Conference night is over. I survived. [deadpan, weary] I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.

lines.text: Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.
lines.script: [brightening, reverent] Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. [direct, sincere] She brings one every conference night.

lines.text: Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.
lines.script: [hushed, conspiratorial] Don't tell Gary. [flat, disapproving] Gary eats the whole thing.

lines.text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
lines.script: [level, eager] Heading out? I can come. [direct, goofy] I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion [deadpan, level] about whatever you're about to fight.

lines.text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
lines.script: [level, dry] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. [rueful, flat] It's been almost done since June.

lines.text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
lines.script: [level, amused] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. [level, direct] I'll be on the ladder.

lines.text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
lines.script: [direct, cheerful] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. [firm, dry] Don't ask about the ladder.

lines.text: Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.
lines.script: [cheerful, relieved] Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. [direct, level] So I came back too. [sheepish, quiet] I brought bread.

lines.text: It's store-bought.
lines.script: [flat, guilty] It's store-bought.

lines.text: Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.
lines.script: [sincere, direct] Take some for the road. [hushed, conspiratorial] Don't tell Gary.

lines.text: Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.
lines.script: [tired, sincere] Every conference night. Twelve years. [dry, flat] It's the only reason Gary shows up.

lines.text: The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [satisfied, level] The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. [sharp, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.text: It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.
lines.script: [proud, bright] It lights up. Every letter. [sincere, mock-offended] I'm an electrician, Gracie. [level, certain] It was never going to just hang there.

lines.text: Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [brisk, distracted] Hold this. No, the other end. [emphatic, quick] It's the OTHER banner. [sharp, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He catches one every time. It's always THIS big.
lines.script: [earnest, hushed] He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. [bright, certain] He catches one every time. [proud, loud] It's always THIS big.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we'd better hurry, before it gets any bigger.
lines.script: [dry, calm] Then we'd better hurry... before it gets any bigger.

lines.speaker: Reel
lines.text: Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. He catches something every day. The size, I round down.
lines.script: [slow, fond] Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. [matter-of-fact] He catches something every day. [dry, knowing] The size, I round down.

lines.text: Here, take my spare cap. For luck. I caught a twelve pounder in it. Nine. It was a big six.
lines.script: [tender] Here, take my spare cap. For luck. [proud, boastful] I caught a twelve pounder in it. [grudging, quieter] Nine. It was a big six.

lines.text: My favorite son!
lines.script: [delighted, warm] My favorite son!

lines.text: My favorite son! And my girls! Come here, come here.
lines.script: [overjoyed, bustling] My favorite son! And my girls! [warm, urgent] Come here, come here.

lines.text: Tom, you must be starving! Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.
lines.script: [warm, fussing] Tom, you must be starving! [brisk, firm] Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

lines.text: My favorite son! And my girls! And my... oh. OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.
lines.script: [delighted, warm] My favorite son! And my girls! [trailing, puzzled] And my... oh. [alarmed, bewildered] OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.

lines.text: Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for the job of a dad. Not even AI wants that!
lines.script: [calm, wry] Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for the job of a dad. [deadpan, tired] Not even AI wants that!

lines.text: Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it.
lines.script: [easy, sheepish] Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it.

lines.text: He's been saying that for a while, babe.
lines.script: [low, dry] He's been saying that for a while, babe.

lines.text: Main event. I'll take it.
lines.script: [amused, easy] Main event. I'll take it.

lines.text: Spooky. I love it. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [amused, uneasy] Spooky. I love it. [cautious, steady] Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles.
lines.script: [focused, murmuring] Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. [soft, delighted] Look at those bubbles.

lines.text: I flew three thousand miles to see you... and maybe the starter.
lines.script: [quickly, warm] I flew three thousand miles to see you... [teasing, low] and maybe the starter.

lines.text: I'm proud. As long as you didn't spin it on your pottery wheel.
lines.script: [dry, mock-offended] I'm proud. [deadpan, grudging] As long as you didn't spin it on your pottery wheel.

lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. So polite!
lines.script: [listing out] Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. [warm, proud] So polite!

lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.
lines.script: [dry, mild] TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.
